intended_object: The canonical R-linear map from the total morphism module ⊕_{(X,Y)∈D×D} Hom_C(F X, F Y) of the quiver induced along F : D → C to the total morphism module ⊕_{(A,B)∈C×C} Hom_C(A,B) of C. On each summand it is the inclusion of the summand indexed by (F X, F Y). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`TotalHom R C` is defined as `⨁ p : C × C, homModule p.1 p.2`. `homInclusion X Y` is `DirectSum.lof` at the index (X, Y). In the induced quiver, the hom module from X to Y is by definition (`rfl`) the hom module of C from F X.obj to F Y.obj. So the map built with `DirectSum.toModule` (the universal property of the direct sum) from the family of summand inclusions `homInclusion (F X.obj) (F Y.obj)` is exactly the intended map. It sends a morphism X ⟶ Y to the same morphism F X ⟶ F Y in the summand indexed by (F X, F Y).

The choice of decidable equality via `Classical.decEq` does not change the resulting map. The library proves the expected properties: the map acts on a single morphism as described, preserves degrees, and is injective when F is injective. The module documentation also correctly notes that the map need not be injective when F is not.

The generality is already natural: any commutative ring R, any graded linear quiver C, and any map of object types F. Mathlib has no graded-linear-quiver framework, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
